memory.calibration: MEASURED 2026-10-05 from generations 149/150, after the n-gram table was converted. THE TABLE IS TP-SHARDED: ngram_embedding is a VocabParallelEmbedding of 320,001,536 x 160, so each rank holds half - 95.37 GiB whole / 47.7 a rank at bf16, 47.7 whole / 23.85 a rank at fp8. ple_gib states the WHOLE table and ple_replicate is false, so the estimate charges half a box, which is what the ranks actually hold. WHY fp8 AT ALL: the checkpoint ships the table as 8 x {packed U8, scales F8_E4M3} plus an F32 global, a layout only the MBX vLLM overlay reads; SGLang skips those tensors by name and leaves the bf16 allocation standing, which is what drove both boxes to 121/122 GiB on generations 146-148. deploy/sglang-27b-tp2/ple-to-fp8 converts them once into the shard_<i>.weight layout SGLang does read, measured at 1.12% mean and 3.78% worst relative error against an independent dequantisation of the source, nothing flushed to zero and no sign errors. THE ARITHMETIC THAT MATTERS: generation 150 reported avail 110.20 GB before the weight load and 24.12 GB after, so 93.3 GiB went to weights 36.89 + the bf16 table 47.7 + about 8.7 of engine - which also says the overhead_gib carried over from the dense SGLang profile (23.7/22.7) OVERSTATES this model by roughly 15 GiB. It is left overstated on purpose: it makes the start estimate stricter, not looser, and one measurement of a model that has never served is not a calibration. Correct it from the first run that completes

tuned.source: MEASURED, 2026-10-05: a four-point sweep of 15-minute deep-research swarms on this profile. gen tok/s over each generation's own perf window: 6 seats/131,072 = 67.4 (400 s, 62 requests); 6/262,144 = 49.0 (891 s, 65); 16/262,144 = 96.2 (920 s, 109); 32/262,144 = 88.8 (893 s, 95). SIXTEEN WINS AND THE FULL 262,144 CONTEXT IS FREE: 16 seats at full context beat 6 seats at HALF context by 43%, so the 27% that looked like a context cost at 6 seats was the pair being decode-starved, not the context. THIRTY-TWO IS WORSE by 7.7%, and the KV pool says why: every seat costs ten GDN slots, so the pool fell from 1,720,000 tokens at 6 seats to 1,482,304 at 16 to 1,140,288 at 32 - at 32 it backs 4.35 requests of full context, so the extra seats buy queueing while taking memory from the cache that would have served them. The next lever is the POOL, not the seat count: mem_fraction_static 0.74 leaves about 24 GB free a box and raising it is untested. Peak 64/66 C at 32 seats, nowhere near the 83-85 C the community 2x-box recipe soaks at. DEPTH 0 IS NOT A TUNING RESULT: the profile keeps its nextn speculative_config because the drafter really is in the checkpoint, but it cannot load on either image - the MTP module allocates its MoE experts at full hidden size while the loader hands it the TP shard, and the start dies in eagle_worker_v2 on a 2560-against-1280 size mismatch (generation 149). Every number here was measured without it, so a default start must be too. Restore the depth when the drafter loads. BUDGET 4,096 is carried from the vLLM profile of these weights and was NOT swept here - it is the one number in this block nobody has measured on SGLang.

memory.calibration: TUNED 2026-10-03 over five generations through the switch (worklog/dflash2-27b-tp2-tuning.md): K=4, not 7 — 201.5 tok/s in total at 8 streams against K=7's 187.6 and K=8's 185.9, because it accepts 0.577 of what it drafts against 0.393 and 0.380, and an exact repeat reproduces the totals to 1.4%, five times the noise. There IS a crossover: at ONE stream K=8 is 33% faster, so a latency-first pair would choose differently. The prefill budget is 4,096, against the engine's own advice: it warns on every start to consider raising max_num_batched_tokens, and 8,192 measured 8.2% SLOWER at 8 streams with acceptance down to 0.530. Under serving load the pair draws 25-27 W a box at 59-63 C; the 60-73 W seen earlier is a ~31-second boot transient on the FlashInfer autotune phase, not a cost of serving. Earlier, 2026-10-02, worklog/dflash2-27b-tp2.md: loaded 61 GiB (box-a) / 56 GiB (box-b) at K=16 against 56/51 at K=0 — +5 GiB a box for the drafter, which is its own 1.92 B checkpoint REPLICATED per rank (mtp_gib), and the BF16 head. The overheads are the dense 27B's, not recalibrated for dflash; the per-seat and per-budget slopes are unmeasured, and a dflash decode step submits 1 + K queries a seat — 48 seats at K=7 is 384 of them, inside the 8,192-token budget, so the budget is not what binds. Seats run to the whole 1..48 this LB allows (MAX_NUM_SEQS_CAP, which mirrors tp-rank's `cmd_up` bound) since 2026-10-02, at the operator's decision; 64 was asked for and is impossible at this pin at ANY context, since 64 seats' fixed_blocks alone are 32.7 GB of a 28 GB pool. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING A 48-SEAT ESTIMATE: the estimate charges nothing for seats 9..48, because concurrency_gib_per_seq is 0.0 here, so nothing pre-flight can refuse a 48-seat start that will not fit. The nearest measured slope in this catalog is Flash-Next's 1.2 GiB a seat (16 to 24) — borrowed, and explicitly NOT this model's measurement: it puts the 40 seats above the anchor at +48 GiB a rank on top of the 61 GiB loaded here, 109 GiB of a 121 GiB box, against the ~4.8 GiB a LOADED box really keeps free. What the pin itself admits is the block rule's, not the seat count's: 49 requests at the 1,024-token minimum context and 3 at the 262,144 default, so past a few seats the pool queues the rest. Measured heat, not modelled: at 8 seats the pair drew 60-68 W a box and box-a went unreachable at 21:03Z, back only by a reboot.

memory.calibration: 2026-10-02/03, worklog/sglang-27b-tp2-c16.md: a verified 16-seat pair (the engine's own max_running_requests=16, no cap) at mem-fraction 0.80 held 61.5 GB of target KV and 19.2 GB of DRAFT KV — DFlash2 runs a second pool — beside ~14 GiB of weights and drafter, for 106 GiB used a box and 14-15 GiB left. SGLang sizes all of that as a FRACTION of the box, not as the absolute pin every other profile here states, so kv_cache_memory below is the measured KV pool itself — 61.5 + 19.2 GB — and engine_args.mem_fraction_static is what the engine is actually told. The first version of this entry set the pin to the fraction's whole share (86.7 GB) and the start was REFUSED at 117 GiB needed on a 115 GiB box (generation 117, 2026-10-03): the fraction covers weights AND KV, while this estimate adds weights and overhead ON TOP of the pin, so stating the fraction's share as the pin counts the weights twice. CORRECTED 2026-10-03 against generation 123's own lines, because the first figures here were the vLLM profile's and the page printed two different token counts for one pool (worklog/sglang-ui-audit.md C3). The engine allocates TWO pools and says so: 'KV Cache is allocated … #tokens: 3415240, K size: 26.06 GB, V size: 26.06 GB' for the target and 'K size: 8.14 GB, V size: 8.14 GB' for the draft — 68.392 GiB together, 73,435,823,273 B, over 3,415,240 tokens, which is 21,502 B a token and NOT the 36,860 of the vLLM profile (SGLang stores KV in fp8_e4m3 and pages at page_size 1). The pin states those two pools, so pin / kv_bytes_per_token reproduces the engine's own token count instead of a number 36% below it. The overheads are back-figured from the same run: 10.28 + 3.58 + 68.4 + 23.7 = 106.0 GiB against the 106 the box held with 15.05 GB free. Per-seat and per-budget slopes unmeasured, as for the vLLM dflash profile. GDN SLOTS (engine_args.mamba_slots_per_req, 10 since 2026-10-03; tp-rank passes --max-mamba-cache-size seats x slots): SGLang carves them out of the same fraction before the KV pools get the rest, so a slot costs 1,824 KV tokens (39,223,296 B a rank) and never box memory - its two committed starts left 21.74 GiB (80 slots) and 21.83 GiB (160) beside the pools (tests/test_memory_estimate.py). The pin therefore stays the TOTAL's figure; the engine's own token count at 32 seats x 10 slots is ~2.89M, not pin / kv_bytes_per_token. Peak draw 35.7 W a box at 63 C with zero throttle microseconds accumulated over the run — roughly half what the same model and drafter drew through vLLM at 8 seats, which is why this profile exists rather than being a curiosity.

traffic.source: Per rank, TP=2, read 2026-10-03 (tests/test_sglang_bandwidth_model.py checks each against SGLang's own allocations). BYTES A PASS STREAMS, off the shard headers on box-c: target = the 64 layers of /srv/models/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (16,891,248,640 B of 2-D+ tensors halved + 1,351,808 B of 1-D ones every rank holds) + half the NVFP4 lm_head (357,580,808) = 8,804,567,176; the embedding shard (1.27e9, gathered by token) and the vision tower (0.92e9, idle on text) are resident and never streamed, which is why memory.weights_gib (10.28 GiB, resident) is not this figure. draft = Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2's attention + MLP halved (QKV/MergedColumn/RowParallel in SGLang srt/models/dflash.py: 3,198,156,800 / 2) + its replicated fc, grouped convs and norms (396,372,480) + the target's lm_head shard its selector projects onto every pass (dflash.py:1097-1124) = 2,353,031,688; the selector's two 248,320 x 256 codebooks are gathered by candidate id. SGLang SHARDS the drafter ('Load weight end ... DFlash2DraftModel ... mem usage=2.25 GB' per rank), so memory.mtp_gib (3.58, the whole file) overstates it here. SHAPES, off the two config.json: 16 full-attention + 48 linear-attention (GDN) layers, 4 KV heads x 256, GDN 48 value heads x 128 x 128; drafter 5 sliding-attention layers, 8 KV heads x 128, sliding_window 2048. DTYPES are the launch's: tp-rank sglang_cmd passes --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 (1 B, the drafter's pool too) and --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 (2 B; the checkpoint says float32).

engine_memory.source: measured 2026-10-24 on this fleet's Radeon 8060S, vexa-stt-rocm sha256:0a7f36742208 (CT2_CUDA_ALLOCATOR=cub_caching), MODEL_SIZE=/models/faster-whisper-large-v3, COMPUTE_TYPE float16, MAX_ACTIVE_REQUESTS 4, the stt node behind the LB: drm-total-gtt of its process (/proc/1/fdinfo) 4,966,568 KiB = 4.74 GiB after 4 concurrent word-timestamped transcriptions of an 84 s file plus a 1200 s whole file. cub_caching keeps what it allocated, so this held figure is the peak

quant_method.source: NVIDIA's released .nemo checkpoint, unquantised (nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 rev 541d1f99c6b0c3cd0b11a95167540bb8edefd82b: parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.nemo 2,509,332,480 B, sha256 3cbdc85877e6…); vLLM never loads it — none

chat.source: a speech-to-text model: it answers an audio upload with its transcript, never a conversation

task.source: a FastConformer-TDT ASR model for 25 European languages, Polish among them, which detects the language itself (model card: Polish FLEURS WER 7.31). On a Polish test set (a CC Spoken Wikipedia reading, clean, under synthetic babble and with a noisy opening; 2026-10-24) it returned 180-187 of ~185 words on every sample, where Whisper large-v3-turbo with its VAD off dropped a 25 s window of clean speech; limits.max_model_len is the lowest the catalog takes: a TDT decoder has no token context

engine_memory.source: measured 2026-10-24 on a GB10, a NeMo 3.0.0 transcription server cutting long files into 300 s pieces — nvidia-smi used_memory of its process, sampled each second: 8,609 MiB = 8.41 GiB decoding a 100 min file alone (the higher of two runs), 7,091 MiB with that file and 3 more word-timestamped requests at once (19 requests, all 200). Pieces decode one at a time (the server's lock), so more seats queue rather than add activations
